candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis requires two distinct components: (1) Diffuse Idiopathic Skeletal Hyperostosis (DISH) as the specific etiology of the confluent multilevel anterior cervical osteophytes (C2–T1), and (2) hypoglossal nerve palsy as evidenced by tongue paralysis with atrophy on cranial nerve examination. C001 acknowledges cervical osteophytes causing dysphagia but does not specify DISH as the underlying condition (versus other causes of osteophytes such as spondylosis or OPLL) and entirely omits the hypoglossal nerve palsy component, which is a required part of the composite benchmark diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures the cervical osteophyte-related dysphagia component but omits the specific DISH etiology and the hypoglossal nerve palsy complication

case_quality_flags: Bilateral pulmonary nodules and mediastinal lymphadenopathy raise concern for concurrent malignancy (e.g., lung cancer given 60 pack-year history), which is not addressed in the reference diagnosis but may warrant separate workup
Tongue atrophy with paralysis localizing to CN XII is a distinctive finding that elevates the diagnosis beyond simple osteophyte dysphagia
